accept.description: what finishing this means — written when the work is asked for, not after

blocked.description: something outside the graph is in the way. A facet, never a status: a blocked task is still open work.

on.description: what it is waiting on, said in words

cancelled.description: the mark a called-off task wears

by.description: who called it off — kept as history when that entity is deleted

via.description: the instrument it was written through — the session or client the write came in on

completed.description: the mark a finished task wears

by.description: who finished it — kept as history when that entity is deleted

via.description: the instrument it was written through — the session or client the write came in on

contains.description: that task is part of this one

requires.description: this task waits for that one

status.description: where the task stands — read off the completed and cancelled marks, never written

statuses.description: every word a task's derived status can be, the host's extra marks included: `wip` is what a task under a live claim reads as, contributed by whoever ships the claim (see MARKS).

task_new.title: File a task
task_new.description: Write down something to do: an entity wearing task{} and doc{title, body}, open by the only definition there is — it wears neither the completed nor the cancelled mark. Say where it is filed and it wears filed{} too.

title.description: what to do, in a line

body.description: the irreducible ask and its pointers, as Markdown

project.description: the project it is filed under

priority.description: queue order — lower is more urgent

assignee.description: whose queue it is filed in

task_list.title: The list
task_list.description: The tasks a query line selects, as whole bundles. `.task` is always on the line; what you say is joined onto it, and saying nothing means `.status=open`. The grammar is the query grammar: `.status=done`, `.filed.project=P-19`, `.priority<3`, a bare word for its text.

task_tree.title: Plan a tree of work
task_tree.description: Write a plan the way the graph holds one: the tasks, and the relations between them, in a single atomic batch. Every node carries a key of its own and says the relation its parent states about it, so nothing is inferred from the order of the list or from prose. dry_run renders the tree and writes neither a task nor a link. Work of three steps or more belongs here rather than in a checklist in one task's body.

project.description: the entity the tree hangs from

key.description: this node's name within the plan — what another node names as its parent

title.description: what to do, in a line

body.description: the irreducible ask and its pointers, as Markdown

status.description: where it stands at birth — open unless said

parent.description: the key of the node it hangs under; left out, it hangs from the project

relation.description: what the parent states about this node — `requires`, `contains`, or any other relation this graph declares

dry_run.description: render the tree and write nothing

task_update.title: Move a task
task_update.description: Change where a task stands or where it is filed. `status` is not a column: done adds the completed mark and drops the cancelled one, cancelled the other way about, and open drops both. Anything you leave out is left alone.

project.description: the project it is filed under

priority.description: queue order — lower is more urgent

assignee.description: whose queue it is filed in
